title: Chapter 264: Plastic Wrap
html:
When they finished the diary, each medical student drew a different conclusion.

“He joined outsiders in abusing his own child. He didn’t deserve to be a father.” Li Xue’s face tightened with anger. Though she knew the Haunted House had probably invented the story, she had become immersed enough to ache for the boy.

“The boy was too weak. If it were me, I would have paid them back twice over!” Wang Dan punched the air.

“I don’t think he was weak. If anything, he frightens me.” Yang Chen studied the diary. “Did you notice that the final months contain apologies only to his father?”

“Doesn’t that prove his weakness? He bowed to the person responsible for everything.”

“He used to apologize to everyone, every day. Then, from one particular moment onward, he wrote only to his father.” Li Xue saw the pattern as well. “Why?”

“Check the dates.” Yang Chen flipped through the earlier entries. Most of the diary’s second half consisted of apologies and penance directed at the boy’s father. “It begins after the school called his father—the night the man beat him until midnight.”

Holding the diary, Yang Chen stood in the center of the room and considered the evidence.

“The entry is explicit. His father locked the room from inside and warned everyone away. He even gagged the boy with a bedsheet. How cruel.” Li Xue’s pity was heartfelt.

“Remember one thing: the boy wrote this diary, so it shows only what he wanted others to see.” Yang Chen closed the book. “Nearly every page contains an apology. Yet this was someone whose entire worldview had inverted, who saw beauty as ugliness and ugliness as beauty. Would such a person truly feel remorse?”

He sat on the reeking bed and placed himself in the boy’s mind. “His classmates hated him, trampled every gesture of kindness, and treated him with disgust. His only family regarded him as an enemy. Violence and rejection filled his life. He buried his true self and used endless apologies as a shield.”

“Yang Chen, what are you saying?” Wang Dan and Li Xue sensed something unusual in his voice.

“I was abused too, but I had a strong, intelligent older brother to protect me.” Yang Chen remained seated. “I understand the boy’s pain. I can guess what he was truly thinking.”

An indefinable emotion filled his eyes. Yang Chen picked up a piece of imitation rubbish. “This Haunted House’s design is remarkable. Everything feels real.”

“Then explain it! Why are you sighing to yourself?” Wang Dan picked up another prop but saw nothing remarkable about it.

“The boss gave us the clue the moment we entered.” Yang Chen sniffed the prop. “None of this rubbish smells, yet the stench remains.”

“Didn’t we establish that earlier?”

“Then have you considered why the boy kept hoarding rubbish?” Yang Chen had uncovered the truth, but solving the mystery brought no thrill—only discomfort.

“Because his mind was warped. Doesn’t the diary prove it? He suffered since childhood until his worldview inverted and ugliness became beauty.”

“Wrong. The answer is much simpler.” Yang Chen turned the prop in his hands. “Real rubbish smells.”

“Real life?”

“The boy used the rubbish to conceal the true source of the stench. That is why he kept bringing it home.” Yang Chen stood and surveyed the room. “What produces a smell that someone would be desperate to hide?”

Wang Dan and Li Xue exchanged a look. As forensic science students, they reached the same answer. “A decomposing corpse.”

“From that night onward, the diary became an endless apology to his father. What did the boy do that demanded so much repentance?” Yang Chen already knew. He approached the room’s only locked wardrobe and reached for its padlock.

The padlock was heavily rusted, but it was only a Haunted House prop. A slight pull tore it free.

The door swung open, and the stench struck like a wave.

A corpse stood inside the wardrobe, encased in plastic wrap.

Its face was contorted and its eyes bulged, preserving the agony of a terrible death. The students stared at the plastic-wrapped body in silence. Horror tightened around their hearts until breathing itself became difficult.

“This is the answer. The boy’s plan began the day he started collecting rubbish.” From that night onward, ten full pages of apologies filled the diary. It was difficult to imagine him spending so long in the room with a corpse.

“The saddest part is that no one discovered the truth. Even after he locked his tormentor in the wardrobe, the boy’s life did not change. No one cared about him. No one even noticed he existed.”

Yang Chen closed the door and replaced the lock. “I’m genuinely impressed that Boss Chen designed a scenario like this. His Haunted House offers more than simple scares.”

“It does.” Li Xue slowly unclenched her hands, though emotion still churned within her.

“Stop mourning over a prop. Twenty minutes must have passed. Let’s move.” The body in the wardrobe deeply unsettled Wang Dan. “The corpses in this Haunted House are more frightening than real ones.”

“Let’s go.” Yang Chen turned first, but stopped at the doorway. “Has the stench grown stronger?”

“Perhaps opening the wardrobe released it.” Li Xue followed him. “Don’t overthink it. We failed today, but we can always return.”

The three left the room and began retracing their steps. A figure now stood in the corridor, facing them with its head bowed and a rope swaying before its neck.

“Isn’t that the hanging mannequin from the first room? How did it get here?”

Wang Dan glanced at his companions and found fear filling both Li Xue’s and Yang Chen’s eyes.

The stench thickened. As the students hesitated, the wardrobe’s padlock slowly worked itself loose and struck the floor.

Creak…

From within, something slowly pushed open the old wardrobe door.
